text:
Jesper Bratt has a point in nine straight games, 9 of the 11 points coming as assists, and that's his season in one line: 4 goals, 18 assists, 22 points in 22 games. He's the Devils' passer, and the passes are working.

The goals are the part that's behind. He has 4 on 6.1 expected (the quality of his chances) and is shooting 8.2%, well below the league's 13.3%. Our numbers flag him as due: he keeps getting the looks. New Jersey takes 61.8% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, which is about as good as it gets for a winger.

Last season said the same thing. Evolving-Hockey had his expected wins (3.2) well above his actual ones (1.9), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 94th percentile for primary shot assists among forwards, with 72% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. A sixth-round pick in 2016, Bratt is now closing in on more Devils franchise marks, per Heavy.com.
headline: Bratt keeps setting the table
